ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The circuit in the figure from left to right is first a sinusoidal voltage source to ground, labeled 5π sin(5000t), followed by a 1 kΩ resistor; the right end of this resistor is node b. A 1 μF capacitor is connected between node b and node a; in the figure, the b side is marked with a negative sign and the a side is marked with a positive sign, so Vab represents Va − Vb. To the right of node a are a 1 mH inductor and a 2 kΩ resistor connected in series in order, finally connected to the upper terminal of a 5 V DC voltage source to ground on the right. Reasoning: The required steady-state average value is the DC component. The DC average value of the sinusoidal source on the left is 0 V, so in DC analysis it can be taken as 0 V. In DC steady state the capacitor is open-circuited, so no DC current passes through this series path, and the DC voltage drops across the 1 kΩ and 2 kΩ resistors are both 0; the inductor is equivalent to a short circuit in DC steady state. Thus node b is connected to 0 V through the 1 kΩ with no voltage drop, so Vb = 0 V; node a is connected to the upper terminal of the 5 V source through the short-circuit inductor and the 2 kΩ with no voltage drop, so Va = 5 V. Therefore the average value of Vab is Va − Vb = 5 − 0 = 5 V.

raw_record.question_text: In the circuit shown, the average value of the voltage \(V_{ab}\) (in Volts) in steady state condition is ______.

method.method_draft: First identify Vab from the image as Va − Vb across the capacitor, positive on the right plate at node a. To find its average in steady state, replace the sinusoidal source by its DC average, 0 V, and analyze only the DC source. In DC steady state the capacitor is open, so no DC current flows through the series path; therefore the 1 kΩ and 2 kΩ resistors have zero DC drop, and the inductor is a short. Thus node b is at the left source's DC value, 0 V, while node a is at the top of the 5 V source, 5 V. Hence average Vab = Va − Vb = 5 − 0 = 5 V.
